External Affairs Minister Resh Jaishankar has called for reform of the U.N. Security Council
saying India and Africa cannot remain underrepresented in the global decision-making.
Addressing a gathering at the Adwa Victory Memorial Museum in Ethiopian capital Adi Sababa,
Dr. Jaishankar called for fair African representation in both permanent and non-permanent membership
and recalled India's efforts during its 2023 G20 presidency to secure permanent
membership for the African Union. India and Africa cannot remain unrepresented in
global decision-making and that is why India worked resolutely during its G20
presidency in 2023 to secure a permanent membership for the African Union.
This decade has seen the UN slide steadily into irrelevance, helpless in
the face of major challenges. Our objective is not merely to add more seats around an old
table. It is to make global governance more democratic, more responsive, and more represented.
And in doing so, make the United Nations itself more capable and more credible.
On the final leg of his three-nation African tour, Dr. Jaishankar urged Indian businesses
to invest in the continent and call for stronger cooperation in food security, agriculture,
and sustainable development.
India has said the proposed interim trade agreement with the United States will be finalized
in light of changing circumstances.
Addressing members of industry chamber, PhD chambers of commerce and industry in New
Delhi today, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Gowal said the framework announced
in February is being reassessed amid changes in the U.S. tariff landscape.
He added that India is seeking more favorable tariff terms to ensure its goods remain
competitive in the American market.
Mr. Goel said India is simultaneously pursuing trade agreements with several partners, including Israel, Chile, the Gulf Cooperation Council and the Eurasian Economic Union.
He said negotiations with Canada are progressing at a faster pace, while talks with the Southern African Customs Union are expected to begin shortly.
Trade discussions with Mexico are also scheduled to commence next week.
The Minister further said the trade ministers of the UK and Canada will visit India next week.
The National Investigation Agency NIA has registered a case to investigate last month's mid-air
cockpit attack on Captain Smith-Marcher aboard a fly Dubai flight.
The case has been registered under the relevant provisions of the Anti-Hijacking Act 2016
and the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act 1967.
Captain Marcher, who hails from Gujarat, was stabbed and seriously injured by his
co-pilot in the cockpit of fly Dubai flight while traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv on
30th of last month. The flight was carrying 174 passengers including 27 children. Several
leaders across the world praised the bravery of Captain Machar who saved the lives of passengers
despite being injured. Several protesters who attempted to reach the protest site at

denied permission for the protest called by CJP. Those who have been detained are
gradually being released. In view of the protests called by the CJP against the Election Commission,

Police officers and personnel, paramilitary personnel have been deployed to prevent any

Special Commissioner of Police Law and Order Devesh Chandrashivasta said that Delhi
police is actively engaging with the public, urging them not to participate in any illegal
protests. He added that it is ensuring that people do not take part in unauthorized protests,
as doing so would be unlawful. He added that it is coordinating with all agencies including
the Central Armed Police Forces and Police Forces from neighboring states to maintain
law and order. Mr. Shrivasta said that overall the situation is fully under control.

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation has informed that 45 metro stations which were closed
from 9pm yesterday due to security reasons will remain closed until 10pm tonight.
DMRC said that the situation will be reviewed further by the security agencies and necessary
updates will be shared accordingly.
A Delhi court today convicted former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain for abetment to rioting in a
case related to 2020 Northeast Delhi riots in the Dayalpur area.
Additional sessions judged Provincing convicted Hussain under relevant sections of the IPC.
The court listed the matter for herring arguments on the quantum of sentence against
Hussain on November 16th. In July, a Delhi court had convicted Hussain and four others
in a case related to the killing of Intelligence Bureau officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020
Northeast Delhi riots. This is Aakashwani giving you the news.

Pradhan Mantri Janadhan Yojana has emerged as a cornerstone of India's financial inclusion

The scheme has provided universal banking access for every household and has become
